the Auger recombination rate in InGaAs quantum wells increases by a factor of 10 as the band gap is increased by 100meV.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Auger coefficient is strongly dependent on the band gap and that this dependence cannot be neglected in the design of high performance InGaAs/AlAsSb lasers.
C increases rapidly with increasing band gap, and hence Auger recombination becomes the dominant non-radiative recombination mechanism in InGaAs quantum well lasers at high temperatures.
Auger recombination is a significant loss mechanism at room temperature, even in low temperature grown quantum wells.
